Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Samir (CSM) -- Laura (CTO - Aegis), Ben (Platform Eng), Ravi (Security), Nina (SRE)

Summary: weekly POC sync for Redwood Private VPC pilot - focus on networking routing quirks, runtime upgrade schedule, and initial latency numbers. Action items at end.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this to about 45 mins. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Laura: Hi, Laura here.
[00:14] Ben: Ben, on the platform team.
[00:16] Ravi: Ravi from security.
[00:18] Nina: Nina, SRE.
[00:20] Maya: Great, Jordan and I from Redwood. Jordan, want to kick off with the metrics you pulled?
[00:28] Jordan: Yeah, sure. So last week's run we did the end-to-end with the VPC peered setup. We saw median latency of 190ms at 1k tokens and p95 around 470ms, which is after we enabled prefix caching on the KV layer. There were a couple of spikes around NAT timeouts.
[00:50] Ben: The spikes coincide with the NAT timeout we have at 30s when the ephemeral connections hit the limit, y'know. We're using shared NAT gateway in the dev account. Could that be the problem?
[01:02] Jordan: Likely. We saw TCP reset around the same timestamps. For the pilot we recommend either move to dedicated NAT or use an interface endpoint so you avoid SNAT explosion.
[01:15] Ravi: Quick question on the routing - do we need to open specific route table entries for the KV cache nodes? Our security team is cautious about opening broader routes.
[01:27] Jordan: Good question. We only need egress to the subnets where the runtime sits and to the KMS endpoint. The route table can be as restrictive as you need; we'll provide the CIDR ranges.
[01:40] Maya: I'll share the exact ranges and sample route table today, should make it easier for your auditors.
[01:46] Laura: Awesome, that helps. Also on the runtime upgrade you mentioned last sync, what is the impact window?
[01:55] Jordan: The upgrade to runtime v2.8 includes kernel selection improvements and better kv-cache eviction. Typical upgrade is rolling per instance, about 3-5 minutes per host for container restart. Planned canary first, then 10% then full. We'll need a brief window where latency may increase; we don't expect failures but we'll have automatic rollback on error.
[02:17] Nina: If we schedule it during our maintenance window, can we pin a canary to a dedicated host instead of mixing with production?
[02:25] Jordan: Yes, we can pin the canary to the dedicated host that we've reserved for your pilot. That will keep your production traffic separate.
[02:32] Ravi: About data residency - are logs or traces leaving our VPC at any point? We need to ensure no PII is sent to Redwood-hosted stacks for this private pilot.
[02:45] Samir (CSM): For Private VPC, telemetry stays in the customer's VPC unless you opt into sending metrics to Redwood console. We can disable remote traces and only send aggregated metrics through the console connector.
[02:57] Ravi: Ok, please send the security doc that states that.
[03:02] Maya: We'll attach the SOC2 and KMS integration doc in the follow-up.
[03:06] Ben: Back to the NAT / routing - if we go with Transit Gateway peer, are there any adjustments on your side? We currently do TGW for inter-account routing.
[03:17] Jordan: TGW is fine; we just need the route propagation to the subnets where the inference hosts live. The only subtlety is with asymmetric routing and path MTU, we've seen a few fragmentation issues on older kernels but v2.8 mitigates some of that.
[03:33] Laura: You mentioned fragmentation - we've seen occasional truncation on larger embedding payloads. Could that be a MTU / fragmentation issue?
[03:42] Jordan: Yes, could be. We recommend setting the MTU to 1400 on the transit peers as a safe start. We'll include that recommendation in the doc.
[03:50] Ben: Can the Redwood runtime report packet and connection metrics so we can cross-check with our VPC flow logs?
[03:58] Jordan: We emit connection-level metrics and error counts to CloudWatch (or your chosen metrics backend); for Private we can configure CloudWatch in your account or push aggregated metrics. We'll share the metric names.
[04:10] Nina: One more on security - KMS integration path: do you support customer-managed CMKs and grant tokens?
[04:18] Maya: Yes, we support CMKs. We'll need the ARN and an IAM role for the inference host to assume. We'll include an example policy.
[04:26] Ravi: Good, provide that example policy.
[04:30] Jordan: Also wanted to call out we ran a quick throughput test: steady-state throughput on your current instance profile gave us ~80 tok/s per host on average for the workload mix you shared. With quantized model u8ddq we get closer to 120 tok/s but that increases small accuracy variance - worth discussing if you want to trade off a bit of quality for cost.
[04:54] Laura: Hmm, accuracy matter for our triage notes. We can't lose more than 1-2% QA accuracy. Do you have evals?
[05:02] Jordan: We do - we'll run the same eval set you provided with the quantized profile and share the diff in the next benchmark run.
[05:08] Ben: Cost - can you provide an estimate if we move from shared NAT to dedicated NAT and vs using interface endpoints?
[05:17] Maya: We'll include cost delta in the pricing doc. Typically interface endpoints are cheaper if you have high egress and avoid NAT per-hour costs; dedicated NAT adds stable throughput but has hourly charge. We'll quantify this in the follow-up.
[05:30] Laura: Any blockers from Redwood's side for the runtime upgrade this week?
[05:35] Jordan: The only blocker is confirming a maintenance window and permission to pin the canary to your reserved host. Once we have that, we can do the canary and share results within 24 hours.
[05:45] Ben: Our ops are free next Tuesday 02:00-04:00 UTC - would that work?
[05:50] Jordan: That window should work. We'll plan the canary at 02:15 UTC to allow pre-checks.
[05:57] Laura: On the topic of routing, we also wanted explicit examples for security: e.g., security group rules and NACLs - we prefer least privilege.
[06:07] Maya: We'll provide a minimal security group example: allow outbound HTTPS to KMS endpoints, allow inbound from your LB CIDR for the admin ports, and lock management ports to your jumpbox IPs.
[06:18] Ravi: For audit, can you provide a mapping of logs to where they are stored and retention? We need S3 bucket policies for logs with encryption.
[06:27] Samir: For the pilot, we'll push runtime logs to a customer-owned S3 with server-side encryption using your CMK. Retention is configurable; we'll document defaults.
[06:38] Ben: Let's talk about failover. If an inference host loses connectivity mid-request, what's the behavior?
[06:45] Jordan: We implement best-effort retries within the request window; we also have automatic fallback to a hosted variant if your Dedicated capacity is temporarily degraded, but that requires opt-in config for data egress. For strict data residency, we can disable hosted fallback.
[07:02] Laura: We'll keep fallback disabled for now.
[07:05] Maya: Understood.
[07:08] Jordan: One other note: we observed a subtle bug where connection reuse wasn't honored with certain ALB idle timeouts - gave an extra handshake. We have a patch in staging that should be included in v2.8. We'll mark that in the release notes.
[07:24] Nina: Any impact to KV cache warmups during restart? We noticed cold-start latency on the first few requests after node restart last week.
[07:33] Jordan: Yes, cold-starts are expected; to minimize we pre-warm hot prefixes based on your usage traces. For pilot we can seed the cache during canary so the canary results are representative.
[07:45] Ben: That would help. Please seed with the last 24h of prefixes we shared.
[07:50] Jordan: Will do.
[07:53] Laura: Ok, let's recap next steps.
[07:56] Maya: Recap: Redwood to share network diagram and route/CIDR lists, SOC2 + KMS docs, planned runtime upgrade schedule and canary details, SE to run the larger benchmark and share logs, AE to send updated pricing with NAT/interface endpoint deltas. Customer to confirm maintenance window and provide CMK ARN and any required cipher list.
[08:20] Ben: Sounds right.
[08:22] Ravi: Also please note security will review the example IAM policy and S3 policy.
[08:28] Maya: Noted. Anything else?
[08:31] Laura: Nothing from me.
[08:33] Nina: All good.
[08:35] Maya: Great, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the canary. Thanks everyone.
